programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc: Edison bulbs are a great design element for your home decor, but the challenge with this trend was a lack of energy-efficient bulbs. But now LEDs have advanced to a point where they are not only energy-efficient but beautiful in these new bulb formats.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: The clients were looking for their forever home when they approached Winter Architecture and Field Office Architecture, and they wanted a home that could be intimate for their family of four but also accommodate entertaining large groups of people. programme.sub-title: A Family's Forever Warm Minimalist Home

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: At Mountainside, there was a natural flow of possibilities emanating from the desert itself. The powerful curves of the granite boulders dominated, yet they were held so gently by golden sands and delicate flora. Looking back, all of this spoke about balance and harmony, and this describes my clients as well.

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Home

programme.sub-title: How To Regrow Scallions From Scraps - Zero Waste Food Tutorial + Harvest

programme.desc: The homeowners love to entertain. Every requirement was about enjoying the Arizona lifestyle while creating a resort-style environment. programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel

programme.sub-title: Ep 3 - Is This The Most Eco-friendly Flight In History | Biofuel + Zero Waste

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel

programme.sub-title: Ep 1 - Sustainability In Thailand | Zeavola Resort, Phi Phi Island

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: This extraordinary, contemporary southwest home located behind the gates of the secluded community of Eagles Nest in Fountain Hills, Arizona is a luxurious, architectural-masterpiece, has 4 bedrooms, 6 bathroom home, with over 8,200 spacious square feet of custom features such as an elevator, air-conditioned garage with custom roll-up glass garage doors, an RV garage, fire and water features throughout, interior and exterior lit stairs and a custom, modern “cloud ceiling”.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Ever wonder how some people get such well-organized mudroom spaces? Sabine walk you through her design choices when it came to the mudroom at The Greenwich House. From lots of cubby storage to a full closet for coats, to why she doesn't like to see hooks on the wall. Get her secrets in this episode of Ideas for Your Home.

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc: We visited the World's Greenest Buildings to see if the design can help save the world. Architects have incorporated nature, renewable technologies, and climate change solutions into their buildings. On the trip, we see the carbon-neutral and eco-friendly design which is helping fight global warming for our future.
programme.sub-title: Green Architecture Saving the World | Visiting Sustainable Buildings from Across the Planet

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc: The Eden Project in England holds the world's largest greenhouse! The project was set up to show its visitors the importance of saving the world's rainforests. In this video, we give you a tour of the indoor rainforest. The project is constructed using huge geodesic domes which hold two biomes. One holds the indoor rainforest and the other holds Mediterranean plants.
programme.sub-title: The Eden Project UK | The Largest Greenhouse In the World

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc: These are the best green school examples from around the world. Each of the examples includes sustainable architecture using eco-friendly building materials. These schools provide children with environmental education and an understanding of how to be more sustainable and eco-friendly. This video features the Green School in Bali, the Copenhagen International School, and the Punahou school in Hawaii.
programme.sub-title: The Most Eco-Friendly Schools | Green Schools Around the World

programme.desc: Melbourne architect, Jerry Wolveridge of Wolveridge Architects, bought the rural property of his clients, and after a study of local agricultural buildings, decided to design a simple, timber-clad pitched off-grid home. Jerry went a step further, adopting the construction methods of Australian sheds, using steel portal frames and avoiding typical "home" materials.
programme.sub-title: An Architect's Own Family Off-Grid Sustainable Home

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Sometimes we get a bit stuck in the past with heritage homes, fixating on the original build year and forget that the home and society has evolved over 140 years. Queen Bess Row was built in 1886, and ZGA Studio wanted to keep the heritage alive and relevant but in a more contemporary world. Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.
programme.sub-title: Keeping the Heritage Alive in this 1880s Home Renovation

programme.title: Simple Dwelling

programme.sub-title: A Home Renovation and Extension that Embraces the Garden

programme.title: Jon Chandonnet
programme.desc: News - Jon Chandonnet was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1996, and as an active grad student at MIT, he responded by pushing his body to the limits. He ran marathons and climbed mountains to prove MS was not slowing him down. Six years later, that pace caught up with him. In this episode, Mathew Embry talks with Jon about denying the diagnosis, what changed when symptoms hit hard, and how MS demands a different kind of discipline. Jon shares how targeting inflammation through diet and lifestyle became a turning point, and how redefining strength has helped him keep moving forward.
